finding.name: Dialect, vocabulary and kind
finding.description: The language that interprets the schema must be explicit: ODCS apiVersion and kind DataContract; JSON Schema $schema meta-schema URI and $vocabulary set; OpenAPI jsonSchemaDialect or OAS dialect id; SHACL Core versus SHACL-SPARQL. Companion JSON Schemas for ODCS and OAS are non-authoritative if they conflict with the standard text.

questions.text: Is this artefact a DataContract, a JSON Schema document, a SHACL shapes graph, an Avro schema, or an OpenAPI Schema Object, and which kind value is declared?
Which meta-schema, apiVersion or dialect URI must a processor load before interpreting keywords?
Which vocabularies are required versus optional, and must a processor refuse the schema if an unknown required vocabulary is declared?
If a companion JSON Schema disagrees with the ODCS or OpenAPI standard text, which source is authoritative?

data_elements.name: Kind
data_elements.description: ODCS required kind; valid value is DataContract. Other families use media type or language name instead of this field.

data_elements.name: Standard version
data_elements.description: ODCS apiVersion of the contract standard used to author the document.

data_elements.name: Schema dialect URI
data_elements.description: JSON Schema $schema or OpenAPI jsonSchemaDialect identifying the meta-schema that the document must validate against.

data_elements.name: Vocabularies in use
data_elements.description: Map of vocabulary URIs to required-or-optional booleans from $vocabulary.

data_elements.name: SHACL profile
data_elements.description: Whether processors must implement SHACL Core only or also SHACL-SPARQL constraint components.

artifacts.name: Declared meta-schema or dialect document
artifacts.description: The meta-schema, ODCS version definition or OAS dialect identified by the contract, used to validate the schema itself.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by the dialect or meta-schema URI, not by local filename.

finding.name: Object and property structure
finding.description: ODCS models a schema as an array of objects, each with a required name and a properties array; each property has a required name and optional logicalType, physicalType, required, unique, items for arrays and nested properties for objects. JSON Schema expresses the same shape through properties, items, prefixItems and applicator keywords; SHACL through node shapes carrying property shapes. Nesting depth, array element typing and the treatment of additional or unexpected properties are the decisions that most often break consumers.

questions.text: What is the full set of objects and properties, including nesting depth and array element definitions?
answer_data: Property list per object with names

questions.text: Is the structure closed, or may an instance carry properties not declared in the contract?
Does property ordering carry meaning for the physical representation, and where is that ordering authoritative?
answer_data: Positional attributes such as key position

questions.text: Which property definitions are reused from a shared definitions library rather than declared locally?

data_elements.name: schemaObject
data_elements.description: A named container in the schema corresponding to a table, view, topic or message type.

data_elements.name: propertyDefinition
data_elements.description: A named attribute within a schema object, carrying type, requiredness and nested structure.

data_elements.name: additionalPropertiesPolicy
data_elements.description: Declared treatment of properties present in an instance but absent from the contract.

artifacts.name: Structural schema definition
artifacts.description: The machine-readable structural definition expressed in the declared schema language.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Registry subject and schema id where a registry is master; otherwise the schema canonical URI; fingerprint over canonical form used to detect duplicates.

finding.name: Composition, references and shape targets
finding.description: JSON Schema applicators apply subschemas in place or to children via $ref, $defs, allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if/then/else, properties, prefixItems and $dynamicRef. $id in a subschema starts a new resource. SHACL distinguishes node shapes from property shapes with sh:path (predicate, inverse, sequence, alternative, quantified paths) and targets class, node, subjects-of and objects-of. Avro references named types by fullname and uses unions instead of oneOf. OpenAPI Schema Object $ref follows JSON Schema 2020-12 inside schemas.

questions.text: Which reusable definitions exist, and which $ref, named-type or shape IRIs must be resolved before evaluation?
How are subschemas combined (allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, union), and does adding a constraint follow open-world JSON Schema rules or Avro field lists?
Which nodes does each SHACL shape target, and what property path is constrained from the focus node?
What happens if a reference cannot be dereferenced, or if $dynamicRef depends on evaluation-time dynamic scope?

data_elements.name: Schema references
data_elements.description: $ref, $dynamicRef, Avro named-type references or SHACL sh:node links.

data_elements.name: Reusable definitions
data_elements.description: $defs (and legacy definitions) or named Avro types available for reference.

data_elements.name: Applicators
data_elements.description: allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if/then/else or Avro union ordered branches.

data_elements.name: Shape targets
data_elements.description: SHACL targetClass, targetNode, targetSubjectsOf, targetObjectsOf or implicit class targets.

data_elements.name: Property path
data_elements.description: SHACL well-formed property path mapping to a SPARQL path.

artifacts.name: Shapes graph or subschema set
artifacts.description: Reusable shapes, $defs and named types that the root schema applies by reference or applicator.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by canonical URI, shape IRI or Avro fullname of each reusable resource.

finding.name: Canonicalization, fingerprints and language alignments
finding.description: Avro Parsing Canonical Form strips docs and aliases, expands fullnames, orders attributes and removes whitespace so two schemas that serialise identically in PCF are the same for readers. Fingerprints of PCF (SHA-256, MD5, CRC-64-AVRO) tag data and cache codecs; they are not security guarantees. JSON Schema $id is an identifier, not necessarily a network locator. OpenAPI Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema 2020-12 with an OAS dialect. Alignments must record conflicts: JSON Schema is open-world constraints; Avro is a closed data definition with positional binary encoding.

questions.text: What canonical form is used to decide whether two schemas are the same for reading, and which attributes are stripped?
What fingerprint algorithm and digest identify this canonical schema, and is it used as a cache key rather than as a security signature?
Which external standards is this contract aligned to, and which semantic conflicts are recorded instead of claimed conformance?
If string-encoded content declares contentEncoding or contentMediaType, is automatic decode disabled by default as JSON Schema requires for safety?

data_elements.name: Canonical form
data_elements.description: Normalised schema text such as Avro Parsing Canonical Form.

data_elements.name: Schema fingerprint
data_elements.description: Short digest of the canonical form used as a tag or cache key.

data_elements.name: Alignment set
data_elements.description: Named external standards and the mapping notes, including known conflicts.

data_elements.name: Content encoding and media type
data_elements.description: JSON Schema contentEncoding, contentMediaType and optional contentSchema for string-encoded payloads.

artifacts.name: Canonical schema and fingerprint record
artifacts.description: Canonicalised schema text plus fingerprint and declared alignments, including conflict notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The fingerprint identifies the canonical bytes; the master-system schema id remains the business identifier.

finding.name: Classification, personal data and usage restriction
finding.description: ODCS carries a classification attribute on properties (for example confidential, restricted, public), a criticalDataElement flag and an encryptedName; the Data Contract Specification carries classification and an explicit pii boolean at field level. These declarations drive downstream access decisions but are not themselves access control: they are the input a policy engine consumes. Retention statements and jurisdictional restrictions belong here as declarations, with enforcement delegated to the access and records-management siblings.

questions.text: What confidentiality classification applies to each property, and from which controlled vocabulary is it drawn?
Which properties carry personal or specially protected data, and on what basis was that determination made?
What protective measures does the contract require for classified properties - encryption, masking, tokenisation or pseudonym columns?
What retention period and deletion obligation does the contract state for the described data?
Are there jurisdictional or residency restrictions on where the described data may be stored or processed?

data_elements.name: propertyClassification
data_elements.description: Confidentiality classification assigned to a property.

data_elements.name: personalDataFlag
data_elements.description: Declaration that a property carries personal data, driving privacy handling downstream.

data_elements.name: retentionStatement
data_elements.description: Declared retention period and deletion obligation for the described data.

artifacts.name: Property classification schedule
artifacts.description: Per-property schedule of classification, personal-data flags, required protection and retention.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Contract identifier plus version plus property path; classification values reference the organisation's governed classification vocabulary rather than free text.
